name: Composite streaming ASR+diar RTF on phone CPU (taskset C0, armed), accuracy byte-identical

description: Attacked the ~8.5 s/stream diar drain: (a) diar-only trailing silence before stream_finish (0/2/4 s) - no effect on the drain, transcript unchanged; (b) skipping stream_finish entirely - saves the whole 8.5 s but changes the transcript (finish also closes the turn still open at end-of-audio), so it is a diarisation change, not a free speedup. Metric unchanged: both flags default to off and stay in the tree as diagnostics.

asi.hypothesis: the 20 s of other_s is a fixed cost inside audiocpp_stream_finish and can be avoided
asi.mechanism_found: NOT overhead. libaudiocpp instrumentation shows the final flush emits ONE window and process_stream_windows spends 8.76 s on it; every window has encoder_frames=188, a FIXED-SIZE encoder pass. The diar costs ~8.5 s per ~26 s window; 'other_s' was simply the last window landing outside the per-piece timers. Short clips pay a whole window for 3 s of audio (7.27 s), which is exactly why it looked like a constant.
asi.probe_a: diar-only trailing silence 0/2/4 s -> drain 8.77/8.97/9.19 s (no effect). Side fact: 2-4 s of trailing silence leaves the transcript byte-identical.
asi.probe_b: skip stream_finish -> drain 0.00, single-pass RTF 0.7849->0.5922 (gate) and 0.7824->0.6578 (chat69), but transcript hash changes on both clips (15/23 blocks either way) - the final decode closes the turn still open at end-of-audio. Rejected under byte-identity.
asi.instrumentation_note: incremental rebuild of libaudiocpp.so for arm64 is 4 s, not the 27 min a full configure costs; ref/audiocpp is a git checkout at fc24c99 so instrument-and-revert is safe and cheap. The instrumented .so must be pushed back out of the device - measure.sh now hash-pushes it.
asi.real_lever: the loop is sequential: push diar (blocks on an 8.5 s window every ~26 s of audio) then accept asr. asr 49.7 s + diar 35.9 s per 228 s of audio, on 2 cores, with the two engines sharing nothing. Overlapping the legs is worth up to min(asr, diar) ~ 36 s per 228 s = RTF 0.47 -> ~0.28 ideal, vs 0.4651 now.
asi.next_action_hint: drive the diarizer from a worker thread fed by a (offset,len) queue into wav.pcm; main thread does asr_stream_accept only; join before the final attribute pass. Output must stay deterministic because speaker tagging happens in the FINAL attribute pass from the complete turn list - verify that assumption holds before trusting the byte-identity result.

description: Ran the diarizer on a worker thread so the two independent legs overlap instead of serialising (asr 49.7 s + diar 35.9 s per 228 s of audio). Rejected on the device: composite got 37-47% SLOWER. Metric reported as unchanged because the async path was reverted (commit daf62f7) and the shipped default path is the baseline tree.

asi.hypothesis: wall = asr + diar because the loop is sequential; overlapping the legs on the 2 A78s should approach max(asr, diar)
asi.result: strongly negative. Paired A/B in one armed window: gate_ms_v2 RTF 0.7848 -> 1.0743, chat69 0.7756 -> 1.1449. Both legs slowed about 2.8x (asr 24.87 -> 70.54 s, diar 20.26 -> 51.63 s) while total CPU work and peak RSS (412 MB) were unchanged.
asi.transcripts: byte-identical sync vs async (md5 db68a9da0e90 / 2929e3cfc15d) - the determinism argument held: tags come from the final attribute pass after joining the worker.
asi.mechanism_best_explanation: superlinear contention between two large streaming working sets (x-asr 168 MB + diar 106 MB) sharing the caches/DRAM bandwidth of the two A78s, plus 8 diar threads + 1 ASR thread on 2 cores. Not a spin-wait livelock, not the GPU path, not affinity (no --main-affinity was passed).
asi.ruling: sequential execution of the two legs is optimal on this device. Predicts any leg-concurrency variant loses; if a future change makes one leg much cheaper, re-test with the CHEAP leg overlapped rather than both.
asi.next_action_hint: structural win is elsewhere: the ASR leg reportedly runs on ONE thread (archive claim), i.e. 49.7 s of the 106 s wall occupies one core while the second core idles, and it cannot be hidden by overlap. Verify thread count on device (NEMO_DEBUG_THREADS prints it per piece) before attacking it.

description: Targeted retry of the leg-overlap dead end (#1082) with the assumption that caused the failure changed: the ASR leg at 1 thread (no 2-thread ggml barrier to spin on) and, in a second variant, each leg pinned to its own A78. Still a loss, so overlap is closed out. Metric is the unchanged baseline because the async path was reverted again.

asi.hypothesis: #1082's 2.8x loss came from a spinning 2-thread ggml barrier competing with diar threads; with ASR at 1 thread the overlap should pay off
asi.changed_assumption: ASR threads 2 -> 1, and a second variant pinned legs to separate cores (mask 0x40 / 0x80 inside the C0 pinning)
asi.paired_chat69_rtf: A sync t=2 0.7773 (reference) | B sync t=1 1.1628 | C async t=1 0.8839 | D async t=1 + per-leg affinity 0.8831 | E async t=2 1.1291
asi.verdict: spin-waiting was NOT the mechanism: async with ASR at 1 thread is still 14% worse than sync. Per-leg affinity changed nothing (0.8839 vs 0.8831) - the --main-affinity/--engine-affinity knobs appear to have no measurable effect at all, which is its own open question.
asi.also_learned: thread scaling is real for both legs: ASR-only chat69 wall 34.83 s at t=1 vs 24.74 s at t=2; diar 31.45 s at t=1 vs 20.44 s at t=2. The -t flag sets BOTH legs' thread counts (bc.threads for audio.cpp, p.n_threads for CrispASR), so 'threads' is not an ASR-only knob today.
asi.build_flags_ruled_out: dotprod already enabled: -mcpu=cortex-a78 implies +dotprod, and the shipped libggml and a forced -DGGML_CPU_ARM_ARCH=armv8.2-a+dotprod+fp16 build contain the SAME 1050+ dotprod instructions. ggml's check_cxx_source_runs probe can never pass when cross-compiling, so the CMake log is misleading, not the binary.
asi.next_action_hint: structural levers exhausted at this model/quantisation. Remaining: (1) prefault the two models at init and check honestly whether it moves work or removes it (measure init_s, not just run wall); (2) KleidiAI matmul backend (build flag, unlikely byte-identical); (3) accept the sequential floor ~0.465.

description: Diar streaming geometry sweep in the *other* direction (chunk_len 510/1020 vs the shipped very_high 340, right context scaled to keep the same overhead ratio). Aggregate is a wash - chat69 -4%, gate_ms_v2 +13% - and the transcript stops being byte-identical on chat69, so it is not admissible. New --diar-session-opt / --diar-opt plumbing kept.

asi.hypothesis: the diar pass costs a fixed ~7 s because the AOS cell's work is the 264-frame speaker cache, not the chunk frames - so FEWER, LARGER chunks should cut the leg
asi.changed_assumption: #1081 measured smaller chunks; this one tests the opposite direction (chunk_len 510/60 and 1020/120 vs the shipped very_high 340/40)
asi.paired_device: gate_ms_v2: base 0.7880 (diar 10.33) | 510 0.8914 | 1020 0.8838 - with diar_s collapsing to 0.01 because the whole clip becomes one window that stream_finish pays for. chat69: base 0.7798 (diar 20.44) | 510 0.7475 (diar 14.37) | 1020 0.7507.
asi.accuracy: NOT byte-identical: chat69 transcript hash changes (2929e3cfc1 -> 2d74b104da at 510, -> 2b99dfc4d6 at 1020) while gate_ms_v2 stays db68a9da0e. Chunk geometry is inert on a 45 s single-window clip and changes speaker tags on a 69 s multi-window one.
asi.verdict: rejected: aggregate is a wash (one clip better, one worse) and it violates byte-identity, which would cost a full paired re-validation for a ~0% gain.
asi.also: found nemotron_3_diar.latency_profile and its session-scoped geometry options (chunk_len/chunk_right_context/fifo_len/spkcache_len/spkcache_update_period in 80 ms encoder frames, graph_arena_mb, weight_context_mb, weight_type). They are SESSION options: setting them on a request fails with 'unknown Nemotron 3 diarization request option'. Added --diar-session-opt K=V for them, and --diar-opt K=V for the request-scoped speaker_* knobs.
asi.stride_note: chunk_len 340 encoder frames = 27.2 s of audio at 80 ms/frame, which is the window length inferred independently from the timing.
asi.next_action_hint: try the memory-sizing session options (graph_arena_mb, weight_context_mb default 1024 MiB each against a 413 MB peak RSS) - numerically inert by construction, so if they move the clock they are free.
